Example 3.2: sires nested in breed, heritability and breed comparisons

Source: R/examples.R
Examp3.2.Rd

Weaning weights of lambs (ex32) with sex, age and breed fixed and sires within breed random: the heritability \(h^2 = 4\sigma_s^2/(\sigma_s^2 + \sigma^2)\), Tukey-Kramer comparisons of the breeds and the predicted breeding values of the sires. The book prints only part of the data, so the numbers differ from those of the book (for this part the sire variance is estimated as zero).

References

Duchateau, L., Janssen, P. and Rowlands, G. J. (1998). Linear Mixed Models. An Introduction with Applications in Veterinary Research. International Livestock Research Institute, Nairobi.

See also

vlm_lsmeans, vlm_blup, ex32

Other VetResearchLMM examples: Examp1.3.2, Examp2.2.1.7, Examp2.3.2, Examp2.4.2.2, Examp2.4.3.1, Examp2.5.1.1, Examp2.5.2.1, Examp2.5.3.1, Examp2.5.4.1, Examp2.6.1, Examp3.1, Examp3.3

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

# SAS program of the book (Appendix B):
#   proc mixed data=ex32;
#     class sex sire_id breed;
#     model ww = sex agew breed / solution ddfm=satterth;
#     random sire_id(breed) / solution;
#     lsmeans breed / adjust=tukey;
#   run;

fm <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = Ww ~ sex + agew + breed
    , data     = ex32
    , random   = ~ breed:sire_id
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = "REML"
    , ddfm     = "satterth"
    , type     = 3
    , class    = "breed"
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
v <- fm$covariance$estimate
h2 <- 4 * v[1] / sum(v)
h2
#> [1] 0
vlm_lsmeans(
    fit    = fm
  , specs  = ~ breed
  , at     = NULL
  , diff   = TRUE
  , adjust = "tukey"
  , level  = 0.95
  )
#> Least-squares means (denominator df: satterth; 95% limits)
